narrative.overview: Conta should feel like a paper account book that happens to run on a phone: a deep ink-blue cover, cool paper pages, a ruled margin, and a red stamp used only when the ledger needs to say something official. The product is ordinary daily finance first, and a bridge demonstration second. Density is calm, numbers are large, and the interface keeps the texture of ruled paper without turning stationery into decoration. The system refuses the generic bank-dashboard grid. Related financial content lives on one continuous sheet, separated by fine rules and internal dividers; tool panels are organized by weight and purpose rather than equal cards. The caderneta is legible from a thumb's distance, honest about demo and native states, and technical detail stays one layer away. Motion is restrained and physical: one route entrance, a stamp that lands, ledger rows that settle, bars that grow, and an activity detail that unfolds. Nothing loops, floats, or competes with the numbers.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-paper ground with a deep ink-blue cover and a single red stamp accent.
Continuous sheets, ruled dividers, and a ruled ledger margin instead of card grids.
Monumental tabular money, quiet metadata, and a compact Geist/Geist Mono pairing.
One authored motion moment per state, with reduced-motion support throughout.

rules.name: The Cool Ground Rule
rules.body: Canvas, paper, and rules stay at hue 248. Warm cream, ivory, and sepia grounds are outside this world.

rules.name: The Stamp Rarity Rule
rules.body: Stamp red is reserved for the demo stamp, destructive/error moments, selected navigation icons, and live marks. It should never become a general-purpose fill or decorative wash.

rules.name: The One Ledger Rule
rules.body: Related financial content shares one paper sheet and is separated by rules. Do not explode one statement into a grid of independent cards.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every monetary figure uses Geist Mono with tabular numerals. The running balance lives in the ledger margin, never as a secondary sentence.

rules.name: The Quiet Metadata Rule
rules.body: Metadata is small, spaced, and uppercase, but it never drops below 0.7rem. If a label needs to be smaller to fit, the content is too dense.

rules.name: The Border-or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A paper surface gets the soft shadow and no border. Do not pair a 1px border with the paper shadow; that recreates the ghost-card look the world refuses.

dos: Do keep related money content on one continuous paper sheet with internal rules.
Do put every amount in Geist Mono tabular and keep the running balance in the ledger margin.
Do keep metadata at 0.7rem or larger.
Do use unequal spans and heights when two blocks have unequal importance.
Do use the stamp red sparingly and keep the rotate at −6°.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion and keep content visible without animation.
donts: Don't build a generic bank-dashboard card grid or give every tool an equal panel.
Don't pair a 1px border with the paper shadow.
Don't use warm cream, ivory, or sepia grounds; the page stays at hue 248.
Don't place kickers or eyebrows above headings.
Don't use hard offset shadows, heavy outlines, or bubbly radii.
Don't use the stamp red as a general fill, gradient, or decorative wash.
